any: The sacristan has rearranged the vestments again and will not say why.
A note in the collection basket, unsigned, about the length of the homily.

Two altar servers did not show, and a third served with his shoes untied.
advent: The Advent wreath was lit by a family whose baby cried through the prayer.
The choir began the Christmas music in the second week, over objections.
The confession line on Saturday went out the door and around the side.
christmas: The midnight Mass was full to the doors and half the faces were strangers.
Poinsettias arrived in quantities no one ordered.
The crib was set up by the Knights, who argued about the placement of the ox.
lent: The fish fry sold out by seven and the Knights blamed the parish next door.
Stations of the Cross on Friday: fourteen people and the smell of wet coats.
A parishioner asked whether coffee breaks the fast, and did not like the answer.
holy_week: The Triduum schedule is on the door in three sizes of type, and still nobody reads it.
The feet for Holy Thursday were volunteered by the same twelve as last year.

easter: The lilies are dying in the sanctuary at a rate that suggests no one is watering them.

First Communion photographs on the steps, in the wind.
flagship_suburban: A parent wants a word about the school's admissions policy.

struggling_urban: The 9:00 had thirty people and the church seats nine hundred.
A man slept in the vestibule and was gone before the first Mass.
immigrant_growing: The 12:30 Spanish Mass overflowed into the hall, where the sound system failed.

rural: The drive to the mission church took forty minutes each way and the heater did not work.
A farmer left a box of sweet corn on the rectory step, with no note.
difficult: Two families are not speaking, and both have told you why.
A letter to the bishop about the parish was copied to you, unsigned.
